concerns.text: FR-004 requires comparing the SYSTEM-GENERATED execution plan against the ground-truth plan, but no task implements the SUT/router plan generator that produces `sut_plan` (required by query_instance.schema.yaml). T021 says 'compute translation errors against T007 ground truth' with no producer of the compared plan, so FR-004 has no implementing task for one of its two operands.

T021 includes 'the ExecutionMetric contract test in tests/contract/test_execution_metric.py', but no task produces the fields that schema requires (`mismatch_flag`, `delta_latency`, `engine_version`, `throttle_config`); the execution_logs.csv columns written by T021 do not include them. Either a task must produce these fields or the contract test references an unimplementable schema — stale coverage.

FR-003 requires 'distinguishing between successful execution and timeout failures', and the Execution Metric entity includes `timeout_flag`, but T021's column list for execution_logs.csv (and execution_log.schema.yaml) has no timeout_flag column; `success_flag=0` conflates timeouts with other failures. No task records the timeout/success distinction FR-003 mandates.

No task implements or references `analysis_result.schema.yaml` (per-group mean_delta_latency, segmented_regression_knee_point, etc.) or `gam_results.schema.yaml` (LMM/Jonckheere-Terpstra). These contracts are orphaned — either add tasks producing their outputs or remove/retire the schemas so implementers don't build unused paths.

US-2 Scenario 2 specifies processing 'a set of 100 high-complexity graph queries' for the error-rate comparison; T025 only aggregates low vs. high groups from the general run. No task fixes the 100-query graph-specific comparison set the scenario describes.

US-1 Scenario 1 pins the environment to '2-core CPU with 7GB RAM limit enforced via cgroups'; T016/T005 implement generic throttling config without recording these specific core/RAM values, so the acceptance scenario's environment is not configured by any task.
